From 531353e650db087e61ce84f8e6b7e0982c1dc1b0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2021 15:57:26 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] iommu: Update "iommu.strict" documentation

Consolidating the flush queue logic also meant that the "iommu.strict"
option started taking effect on x86 as well. Make sure we document that.

Fixes: a250c23f15c2 ("iommu: remove DOMAIN_ATTR_DMA_USE_FLUSH_QUEUE")
Signed-off-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/2c8c06e1b449d6b060c5bf9ad3b403cd142f405d.1623682646.git.robin.murphy@arm.com
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>

diff --git a/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt b/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
index cb89dbdedc46..20a32de990ed 100644
--- a/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
+++ b/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
@@ -1987,7 +1987,7 @@
 			  forcing Dual Address Cycle for PCI cards supporting
 			  greater than 32-bit addressing.
 
-	iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
+	iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
 			Format: { "0" | "1" }
 			0 - Lazy mode.
 			  Request that DMA unmap operations use deferred
@@ -1998,6 +1998,10 @@
 			1 - Strict mode (default).
 			  DMA unmap operations invalidate IOMMU hardware TLBs
 			  synchronously.
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict
+			mode explicitly specified by either method takes
+			precedence.
 
 	iommu.passthrough=
 			[ARM64, X86] Configure DMA to bypass the IOMMU by default.
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt**
   - The documentation for the `iommu.strict` kernel parameter has been updated to reflect that it now applies to both ARM64 and x86 architectures. 
   - The description was changed from:
     ```
     iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
     ```
     to:
     ```
     iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
     ```
   - Additional notes were added to clarify that on x86, the default behavior is influenced by driver-specific parameters, but that explicitly specifying strict mode takes precedence.

### Relationships

- The changes in the documentation are directly related to a previous modification in the codebase (referenced by the Fixes tag) that consolidated flush queue logic, which allowed the `iommu.strict` option to take effect on x86 systems. This patch ensures that the documentation accurately reflects the current behavior of the `iommu.strict` parameter across both ARM64 and x86 architectures.

Here is the commit message:
iommu: Update "iommu.strict" documentation

Consolidating the flush queue logic also meant that the "iommu.strict"
option started taking effect on x86 as well. Make sure we document that.

Fixes: a250c23f15c2 ("iommu: remove DOMAIN_ATTR_DMA_USE_FLUSH_QUEUE")
Signed-off-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/2c8c06e1b449d6b060c5bf9ad3b403cd142f405d.1623682646.git.robin.murphy@arm.com
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of documentation regarding the applicability of the `iommu.strict` option to the x86 architecture. Previously, the documentation only mentioned ARM64, which could lead to confusion about the behavior of the option on x86 systems, especially after the flush queue logic was consolidated to include x86. This oversight could result in users not understanding how to configure TLB invalidation behavior correctly on x86.

Here is the patch:

-	iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
+	iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
 			Format: { "0" | "1" }
 			0 - Lazy mode.
 			  DMA unmap operations invalidate IOMMU hardware TLBs
 			  synchronously.
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict
+			mode explicitly specified by either method takes
+			precedence.
 
 	iommu.passthrough=

```c

```
Reason:
The documentation only specified the `iommu.strict` option for ARM64, which created confusion regarding its applicability on x86 systems. This oversight could mislead users into incorrectly configuring TLB invalidation behavior on x86, especially after the flush queue logic was consolidated to include x86.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict mode explicitly specified by either method takes precedence.
```
Reason:
The patch updates the documentation to explicitly include x86 in the `iommu.strict` option, clarifying its applicability. Additionally, it provides important information about the default behavior on x86 systems, ensuring users understand how to configure TLB invalidation correctly.
